title: Route Controls: Quantization enablement config examples + migration notes + common validation errors
content:
Purpose
- Working collection of examples + gotchas for enabling Quantization Profile Library by route.
- Intended audience: platform engineering + oncall + solutions engineering. Not customer-facing.
- This doc is intentionally redundant with Confluence; Drive version is more “copy/paste friendly” and includes troubleshooting.

Scope
- Route-level enablement/disablement + canary controls.
- Precedence rules (org vs customer vs route).
- Migration from older model-scoped flags.
- Common validation errors and how to fix them.

Non-goals
- How to build a quantization profile (Applied ML owns).
- How runtime resolves profile artifacts (runtime owns).

Terminology (quick)
- Baseline: default (fp16/bf16) kernel path.
- Quantized path: int8/int4/etc using a published profile from model registry.
- Route: named API route/workload configuration (e.g., "interactive-chat", "batch-summarize").
- Org config: default settings at org/account level.
- Customer override: per-customer settings (rare; enterprise exceptions).
- Route config: settings applied to a specific route. This is the primary control surface for v1.
- Canary: percentage-based gate to send a slice of traffic down quantized execution.

Precedence (as implemented in policy evaluation)
1) Explicit customer override (if present) takes precedence over everything.
2) Route settings (within an org) override org defaults.
3) Org defaults apply if no route settings exist.
4) If none exist: quantization is DISABLED by default (opt-in).

Important: “disable” beats “enable”. If any higher-precedence config explicitly disables quantization, we do not quantize.

Common fields (conceptual model)
NOTE: actual wire schema differs between Hosted control plane (JSON via Console API) vs Dedicated/Private (config file). Examples below show both.

Quantization settings fields (conceptual)
- enabled: true|false
- mode: "auto" | "pinned" (auto lets runtime pick best compatible profile; pinned pins a specific profile id/version)
- canary_percent: 0..100 (integer)
- pinned_profile_id: string (required if mode=pinned)
- pinned_profile_version: string (semver; optional if mode=pinned; if omitted, latest compatible)
- allow_models: optional list (guardrail; if set, only these model ids can be quantized on this route)
- deny_models: optional list (guardrail)
- fail_open: true|false
  - false: if quantization can’t be applied (no compatible profile / incompat HW), run baseline and emit reason tag (default)
  - true: NOT ALLOWED for Hosted (kept for internal testing only; rejected in validation)

Audit logging
- Any change to route-level quantization settings MUST emit an audit event.
- Expect fields in audit event: actor, org_id, route_id, before, after, request_id.


====================
A) Hosted API / Control Plane examples (Console API)
====================

A1) Enable quantization on a single non-interactive route (batch summarization)
Use case: Customer wants cost reduction; willing to accept small quality risk on background jobs.

PATCH /v1/orgs/{org_id}/routes/{route_id}/quantization-settings
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "enabled": true,
  "mode": "auto",
  "canary_percent": 100
}

Notes:
- In “auto” mode, runtime chooses best compatible profile for the requested model/hardware.
- We still do safe fallback to baseline if no compatible profile exists.

A2) Canary rollout to 10% for interactive workloads (recommended first step)

{
  "enabled": true,
  "mode": "auto",
  "canary_percent": 10
}

Operational note:
- Canary is evaluated in policy engine (stable hashing on request id / trace id). Mixed traffic is expected.
- Watch: format regressions (JSON mode), tool-call validity, and long-context latency.

A3) Pinned profile (only when you need absolute repeatability)

{
  "enabled": true,
  "mode": "pinned",
  "pinned_profile_id": "qpl:llama-3.1-70b:int8:rtx-l40s",
  "pinned_profile_version": "1.3.0",
  "canary_percent": 100
}

Notes:
- Pinned is stricter and can reduce “surprises”, but increases operational work when we rev profiles.
- If the pinned profile becomes incompatible in a region/cluster (GPU SKU mismatch), runtime falls back to baseline and emits a metric tag (see “Troubleshooting”).

A4) Disable quantization explicitly on a route (hard off)

{
  "enabled": false
}

Notes:
- Useful for “must be perfect” routes: auth flows, tool-calling/JSON critical routes, compliance exports.

A5) Model allowlist guardrail (recommended for multi-model routes)
Scenario: Route can call multiple models; you only want to quantize a subset.

{
  "enabled": true,
  "mode": "auto",
  "canary_percent": 50,
  "allow_models": [
    "llama-3.1-8b-instruct",
    "llama-3.1-70b-instruct"
  ]
}

Behavior:
- If request targets a model not in allow_models, route runs baseline.

A6) Customer override example (exception handling)
Use sparingly (enterprise contracts / known workload constraints).

PATCH /v1/orgs/{org_id}/customers/{customer_id}/quantization-override
{
  "enabled": false,
  "reason": "JSON mode regressions observed on customer prompt set; disable until profile >=1.4.x validated"
}

Notes:
- Overrides apply across routes unless override is route-scoped in the payload (TBD; do not assume).
- Make sure support + CSM are aligned; this impacts perceived performance/cost.


====================
B) Dedicated / Private examples (config-file style)
====================

B1) Dedicated cluster: org defaults + per-route override
File: redwood-control-plane.yaml

org_defaults:
  quantization:
    enabled: false

routes:
  - id: batch-summarize
    quantization:
      enabled: true
      mode: auto
      canary_percent: 100

  - id: interactive-chat
    quantization:
      enabled: true
      mode: auto
      canary_percent: 5

Notes:
- Dedicated generally has more predictable GPU SKUs; still do not assume compatibility.
- If customers have both L40S + A100 pools, ensure profiles are scoped per GPU arch.

B2) Private (VPC/on-prem): pinned profile for a specific GPU class
File: routes.yaml

routes:
  - id: internal-agent-tools
    quantization:
      enabled: true
      mode: pinned
      pinned_profile_id: qpl:qwen2.5-32b:int4:sm90
      pinned_profile_version: 0.9.2
      canary_percent: 100

Notes:
- Private deployments often require deterministic behavior for auditability.
- Ensure artifact signing verification is enabled; if signature verification fails, route MUST run baseline.

B3) Private: denylist long-context route (avoid long-context perf regressions)

routes:
  - id: long-context-analysis
    quantization:
      enabled: true
      mode: auto
      canary_percent: 100
      deny_models:
        - llama-3.1-70b-instruct

Notes:
- This is a pragmatic workaround for cases where quantization helps short prompts but hurts long context.
- Prefer a profile scoped to the long-context regime once available.


====================
C) Migration notes (from legacy model-scoped flags)
====================

Background
- Older configuration patterns used model-scoped toggles (e.g., “enable int8 for model X”) or environment flags at the gateway.
- v1 design is route-first: quantization is an optimization decision tied to workload, not just the model.

What to remove / stop using
- Any global flag that changes quantization behavior without an audit trail.
- Any per-request header override used outside of internal testing (see API conventions doc). If the header exists in prod and conflicts with route config, route config wins.

Suggested migration steps (safe)
1) Identify candidate routes (start with batch/offline): batch summarization, document chunking, embeddings rerank (if applicable).
2) Create route configs with enabled=true, canary_percent=1 or 5.
3) Validate cost/latency + quality metrics segmented by route_id and quantization_mode.
4) Increase canary to 25 -> 50 -> 100, waiting at least N hours and checking:
   - output format correctness (esp. JSON mode)
   - tool-call validity (schema match rate)
   - 5xx/429 changes
   - p95 latency and time-to-first-token (TTFT)
5) Remove legacy model-scoped toggles after route configs are stable.
6) Document the chosen behavior in the customer’s runbook (esp. if they have “must-not-quantize” routes).

Rollback plan (quick)
- Set enabled=false at the route level. Do NOT delete the route object (keep for audit trail).
- For Dedicated/Private, apply config change and reload control plane; verify worker caches refresh.


====================
D) Common validation errors (and fixes)
====================

D1) canary_percent out of range
Error:
- "quantization.canary_percent must be an integer between 0 and 100"
Fix:
- Use 0..100 integer only. No floats.

D2) mode=pinned but missing pinned_profile_id
Error:
- "pinned_profile_id is required when quantization.mode is 'pinned'"
Fix:
- Provide pinned_profile_id (and optionally pinned_profile_version). If you don’t want to pin, use mode=auto.

D3) Unknown pinned_profile_id / not published
Error:
- "profile not found" or "profile_id not recognized"
Fix:
- Verify profile id exists in model registry and is in the Quantization Profile Library namespace (qpl:*).
- If you got the id from a spreadsheet/notes, confirm it was actually published + signed.

D4) Profile exists but is not compatible with hardware
Symptoms:
- Request runs baseline; metrics show quantization_apply_reason="incompatible_hardware".
- Some clusters/regions quantize and others do not.
Fix:
- Use mode=auto to let runtime pick compatible profile per GPU.
- If pinned is required, pin a profile scoped to the GPU arch in that cluster.

D5) Conflicting allow_models and deny_models
Error:
- "allow_models and deny_models are mutually exclusive" (or) "model appears in both lists"
Fix:
- Choose one approach; prefer allowlist for safety.

D6) Attempted fail_open=true on Hosted
Error:
- "fail_open is not permitted in hosted control plane"
Fix:
- Remove fail_open; Hosted always fails closed to baseline.

D7) Route not found / route_id invalid
Error:
- "route_id does not exist" or "cannot modify system route"
Fix:
- Ensure route exists and is customer-configurable.
- Some system routes are immutable (internal).

D8) RBAC / permission denied
Error:
- 403 "insufficient permissions to modify quantization settings"
Fix:
- Request the correct Console role or API scope. Changes should be limited to Org Admin / Platform Admin roles.

D9) Validation rejects changes due to active incident lock (SRE safety)
Error:
- 409 "configuration changes blocked (incident mitigation mode)"
Fix:
- Coordinate with oncall (eng-sre). Apply changes via the emergency override process if needed.


====================
E) Troubleshooting checklist (ops)
====================

If a route is enabled but you’re not seeing cost improvements:
- Confirm canary_percent=100 and enabled=true.
- Confirm metrics tag execution_mode=quantized is present for that route.
- Check apply_reason tags: "no_profile", "incompatible_hardware", "policy_disabled", "model_not_allowed".
- Check model mix on that route (if allow_models set, maybe most traffic is to another model).
- Check sequence length distribution: some profiles only help short contexts.

If 5xx increases after enabling:
- Immediately set enabled=false on affected route(s).
- Look for incompatibility loops: repeated profile refresh attempts, cache stampede symptoms.
- Verify you’re not pinned to a profile that is missing in one region.

If output format regresses (JSON mode / tool calls):
- Disable quantization for that specific route (don’t blanket disable for org unless necessary).
- Add the route’s prompt set to quantization eval coverage plan (Applied ML).


Open questions / TODO (platform)
- Do we want route-scoped customer overrides (customer override only applies to one route vs whole org)? (needs product input)
- How we represent long-context regime selection in policy config (currently runtime-only heuristics).
- Document the exact metric names used for segmentation once telemetry naming stabilizes (Logan/Nadia to confirm).
